I have been working this land for 25 years, so I know what works here in Quzhou. My 50 mu is big enough that I have to plan carefully — running out of fertilizer at the wrong time costs real money, and on this much land small mistakes add up fast.

For my cotton, I will plant about 20 mu. I use improved Bt cotton seed because the bollworm problem is serious and the old varieties get eaten alive — everyone around me switched years ago. Last year I put on about 15 kg of urea worth of nitrogen per mu, and the bolls were good, so I will do the same — maybe 16 kg N per mu. Phosphorus I put in as base fertilizer with diammonium phosphate, around 8 kg per mu. Potassium I learned matters for boll filling, so 10 kg per mu. I will irrigate 4 times from the well — before planting, at squaring, at flowering, and at boll-forming. Pesticide I have to spray maybe 5 times, mostly for aphids and mirid bugs since Bt handles bollworm. I plough the cotton field deep because cotton likes loose soil. I expect around 280 kg seed cotton per mu if the weather holds.

For stevia, I will plant 30 mu — Quzhou is good stevia country and the buyers come here. I use improved transplants from the company that buys the leaves, they give better sweetness. Stevia wants more potassium than nitrogen for good leaves, so I put 14 kg N, 7 kg P, 14 kg K per mu. I irrigate 6 times because stevia needs steady water for leaf growth and I cut it twice. Pesticide maybe 3 times — stevia has fewer bugs than cotton. Rotary tillage is enough since I transplant seedlings. I expect 280 kg of dried leaves per mu across two cuts.

I follow what worked last year — Bt cotton with moderate nitrogen and deep plough, and stevia with more potassium for leaf quality and more irrigation for steady growth.
